title: Building agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

questions.prompt: Which frameworks and models can you use with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore?
questions.explain: AgentCore works with any open source framework, such as CrewAI, LangGraph or Strands, and with any foundation model.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore overview

questions.prompt: How do the docs describe the hosting environment of AgentCore Runtime?
questions.explain: Runtime is a secure, serverless, purpose-built hosting environment for AI agents and tools, so you do not manage servers.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Runtime

questions.prompt: In AgentCore Runtime, what does each user session run in?
questions.explain: Each session gets a dedicated microVM with isolated compute, memory and filesystem. When the session ends, the microVM is terminated and memory is sanitized.
questions.subtitle: Session isolation

questions.prompt: How long can an AgentCore Runtime session run on microVMs?
questions.explain: Runtime sessions run for up to eight hours on microVMs, or up to fourteen days on Instances. That suits long-running, asynchronous agent work.
questions.subtitle: Long-running sessions

questions.prompt: Which protocols can Runtime agents use to talk to other agents and tools?
questions.explain: Runtime lets agents communicate with other agents and tools through the Model Context Protocol, MCP, or Agent to Agent, A2A.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Runtime

questions.prompt: What does AgentCore short-term memory capture?
questions.explain: Short-term memory captures turn-by-turn interactions within one session, so users do not have to repeat themselves.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Memory

questions.prompt: Which AgentCore memory type keeps key insights across multiple sessions?
questions.explain: Long-term memory automatically extracts and stores insights such as preferences, facts and summaries, and keeps them across sessions.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Memory

questions.prompt: Which memory strategy learns a customer's preferred shipping carrier?
questions.explain: The user preference strategy extracts preferences, choices and styles, such as a preferred shipping carrier, and builds a profile of each user.
questions.subtitle: Memory strategies

questions.prompt: Which memory strategy condenses a session into key topics, tasks and decisions?
questions.explain: The summary strategy produces condensed summaries of a single session, covering its key topics, main tasks and decisions.
questions.subtitle: Memory strategies

questions.prompt: Which memory strategy creates reflections, insights drawn from many past episodes?
questions.explain: The episodic strategy records meaningful episodes, then generates reflections across them. Those reflections help the agent repeat what worked and avoid past mistakes.
questions.subtitle: Memory strategies

questions.prompt: AgentCore Gateway turns your APIs and Lambda functions into what?
questions.explain: Gateway converts APIs, Lambda functions and existing services into tools that work with MCP, and it accepts OpenAPI, Smithy and Lambda as tool inputs.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Gateway

questions.prompt: How does Gateway help an agent pick the right tool among thousands?
questions.explain: With semantic tool selection, agents search the available tools for the best match to the task. This keeps prompts small and lowers latency.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Gateway

questions.prompt: In AgentCore Identity, where are OAuth tokens and API keys stored securely?
questions.explain: The token vault stores OAuth tokens, client credentials and API keys, encrypted with KMS keys. Only an agent that proves its workload identity can read them.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Identity

questions.prompt: Which kind of authentication lets an agent call services like Slack or GitHub?
questions.explain: Inbound auth decides who can call the agent. Outbound auth lets the agent reach third-party services like Slack, Zoom and GitHub with OAuth or API keys.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Identity

questions.prompt: In which standard format does AgentCore Observability emit telemetry?
questions.explain: AgentCore emits OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry, and stores its metrics, spans and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. You can also connect your existing monitoring stack.
questions.subtitle: AgentCore Observability

questions.prompt: Which AgentCore built-in tool lets an agent run Python securely in a sandbox?
questions.explain: Code Interpreter lets agents write and run code in isolated sandboxes. It supports Python, JavaScript and TypeScript.
questions.subtitle: Code Interpreter

questions.prompt: Runtime session data is temporary. Where should learned user preferences go for later sessions?
questions.explain: By default, a session's compute is temporary. For data that must outlast the session, such as learned preferences, the docs recommend AgentCore Memory.
questions.subtitle: When to use which

questions.prompt: Your agent must navigate a website and fill in forms. Which AgentCore service fits?
questions.explain: AgentCore Browser is a secure, isolated cloud browser for agents. Agents use it to navigate sites, click elements and fill forms, and you can watch with Live View.
questions.subtitle: When to use which
